text:
amira: Spiked an alternative to the preproc-sidecar idea: make the sidecar a tiny runtime that runs sandboxed transform modules (WASM by default). Rationale: lets product/solutions ship tenant-specific rules without changing service code, and keeps transforms isolated for security. Thoughts?

jon: Interesting. WASM means we can run deterministic transforms across languages. Main concerns: cold-start of modules, and verifying module provenance.

priya: +1 for sandboxing. We should require modules to be signed and stored in an immutable artifact registry. Sidecar would fetch by version tag and verify signature before loading.

amira: Agreed on signing. Also planning that modules are small (<= 200KB), with a short init path and a re-use pool to avoid repeated cold start costs. If module load exceeds X ms, sidecar should fall back to the last-good module.

jon: How would we express transforms? Need a minimal host API: access to tokenizer hints, a replace/patch API, and an append metadata envelope. Example host API: 
```
apply_transform(module, {tenant_id, raw_prompt, profile_hint}) -> {output, patches, metrics}
```
We should avoid exposing network calls from modules.

priya: Keep module surface tiny. No outbound network. File/DB access should be blocked. Logging only via host-provided console that attaches tenant and request id.

amira: Rollout consideration: modules are versioned like semver (v1.2.0) and bound to tenants via profile registry. Plan for a mirror-canary: run new module in read-only mode alongside the active module for a sample percent of traffic, compare outputs via diff, and monitor "module_mismatch_pct".

infra-bot: Note: added k8s job template for registry sync and a Helm chart stub for sidecar with a configmap mount for trusted public keys.

jon: Perf targets: local sidecar (unix socket) p50 < 0.8ms, p99 < 3ms with common modules. Remote shared pool target p50 < 2ms, p99 < 8ms. We'll need microbenchmarks by module complexity.

priya: Observability: emit transform_version, module_signature_id, transform_time_ms, mismatch_flag, and patch_count. Also traceable spans that include module load time. Important to tie outputs to the tenant's model-profile version.

amira: Error modes: 1) module panics -> host unloads and increments "module_crash_count" and falls back; 2) signature mismatch -> reject load; 3) semantic mismatches during canary -> auto-disable new module for that tenant. These rules in the RFC.

jon: Migration path for legacy regex rules: create a compatibility shim that compiles old regex bundles into WASM at deploy time. That gives us parity for a fast cutover.

priya: Security ops: need automated signing keys rotation, an audit log for module publishes, and an allowlist for tenants that can enable custom modules. Default hosted tenants get only vetted modules from Redwood store.

amira: Operational model: Dedicated customers can opt for a colocated sidecar container per node (unix socket) to hit the low-latency path. Hosted customers default to a shared sidecar pool behind an autoscaled service with sticky routing by tenant for cache locality.

ops-bot: Created runbook entry: /runbook/wasm-preproc-sidecar  steps: module publish, canary mirror, rollback, emergency disable. Linked to playbooks for signature-key roll / tenant opt-out.

jon: SDK change: response from preproc should include transform_version and module_id so clients can log/trace. Also add a dry-run endpoint for product teams to validate transforms against a prompt corpus.

priya: Testing: unit tests inside module builds, plus fuzz corpus and offline regression tests. We should add an integration test that runs the sidecar + runtime with latency injection and failure injection.

amira: I'll draft RFC this week covering: interface contract (host API), signing and registry, runtime lifecycle semantics, canary thresholds (mismatch > 0.2% => rollback), perf targets, and deployment modes. Reviewing needed from security, infra, and product.

jon: Minor ask: add a metric for "module_cache_hit_rate" to ensure we tune eviction.

priya: Also document SLO impacts when shared pool p99 climbs; define per-tenant fallback to runtime-native transforms for safety.

amira: Thanks. If no objections I'll post RFC draft by EOD and schedule a quick sync with sec/infra tomorrow.

infra-bot: RFC calendar invite created: /events/wasm-preproc-rfc-review 30m tomorrow 09:30.

ops-bot: Checklist updated: dashboards + alerts (mismatch_pct, preprocess_latency_p99, module_crash_count), runbook link included.
